description: Fetch observations for up to 3 ILOSTAT datasets per call, filtered by reference area or area group, sex, breakdown codes (classif1, classif2), source, and period; datasets past the first 3 come back as remaining_dataset_ids for another call. Rows keep their source, observation status, decoded notes, and a basis — reported, modelled_estimate, or projection — and the response echoes every filter applied, including the best-source default. Codes are checked against ILOSTAT's dictionaries before the request is sent: ilostat_list_reference lists valid codes and ilostat_describe_indicator lists the codes a dataset actually uses. Rows come back limit at a time from offset, and next_offset continues the same request; on the first page, a result past the staging threshold is also staged in full as a df_<id> dataframe for SQL through ilostat_dataframe_describe and ilostat_dataframe_query when this deployment enables dataframes. A request with no filters at all is refused when the dataset exceeds the row ceiling; a filtered result past the ceiling is paged but not staged, and a page reaching past the ceiling is refused with guidance to narrow the request.

area_group.description: X01 for every country, an ILO region or subregion, or a World Bank income group (X06, X56, X02, …); expands to its member countries, unioned with ref_areas. ilostat_list_reference topic area_groups lists the codes.

classif1.description: Codes of the first breakdown (e.g. AGE_YTHADULT_YGE15); case-insensitive. ilostat_describe_indicator lists the codes a dataset uses.

classif2.description: Codes of the second breakdown, for datasets that have one; case-insensitive. ilostat_describe_indicator lists them.

dataset_ids.description: Dataset IDs, up to 100 — an indicator code plus _A, _Q, or _M (UNE_DEAP_SEX_AGE_RT_A), as ilostat_search_indicators returns them. Case-insensitive; a DF_ prefix (the SDMX dataflow form) is stripped, a bare indicator code resolves when it has one frequency, an element holding + or , joined IDs is split, and duplicates are dropped. Every ID is checked; the first 3 distinct datasets are queried and the rest come back as remaining_dataset_ids for another call.

latest_only.description: Only each series' latest period — a series is one dataset, reference area, sex, classif1, and classif2 code — with every row at that period (one per source under source_selection all or secondary; the latest quarter or month on sub-annual datasets); combines with time_from/time_to. When the request's full history is too large or too slow to read in one call, it falls back to the latest period per area and dataset, which can miss a series that ends earlier; applied_filters.latest_mode says which ran, and the notice says so. time_from or classif1 narrow it back under; sex or fewer ref_areas alone may still read too much and fall back.

limit.description: Rows per page, at most 5,000; a larger value is applied as 5,000 and the notice says so.

offset.description: Rows to skip: 0 for the first page, else the previous page's next_offset, with the same other arguments. Each page re-reads the request upstream; under latest_only, combine pages only when their applied_filters.latest_mode matches.

ref_areas.description: Reference areas (up to 300): ISO3 country codes (USA) or X-coded aggregates (X01 World); case-insensitive, ILO_GEO_ forms accepted. Aggregates need a dataset with has_aggregates true. Omit for every area.

sex.description: Sex codes SEX_T, SEX_M, SEX_F, SEX_O; T/M/F/O and total/both/male/female/other are accepted.

source_selection.description: best (default): the preferred source per area and period; all: secondary sources too, each row flagged best_source; secondary: secondary sources only. Defaults to all when sources is set.

sources.description: Source codes (e.g. BA:453); ilostat_list_reference topic sources with ref_area lists an area's sources. Without source_selection, setting sources switches it to all, since a secondary source matches nothing under best.

time.description: One exact period: YYYY (on a quarterly or monthly dataset, every period of that year), YYYYQn, or YYYYMmm; 2024-Q2, 2024 Q2, and 2025-03 are normalized. Not combinable with time_from, time_to, or latest_only.

time_from.description: First year (YYYY); upstream filters by year only.

name: ilostat_query_indicator

applied_filters.description: Every parameter sent upstream, defaults included.

area_group.description: The area group and how many countries it expanded to.

latest_mode.description: How latest_only was answered: per_series, each series' own latest period; latest_year, the fallback to the latest period per area and dataset, which can miss a series that ends earlier. Absent without latest_only.

latest_only.description: Whether only each series' latest period was requested.

ref_area_count.description: Areas sent upstream: ref_areas plus the area_group members.

source_selection.description: Source selection applied (all when sources were given without one).

attribution.description: Citation to keep with any use of the data.

cap.description: The limit applied to this page.

dataframe.description: The staged dataframe holding the full result; present only when staged.

evicted.description: Dataframes dropped, oldest first, to keep this tenant within 1,000,000 staged rows and 100 dataframes; present only when staging this one evicted any.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 expiry of the staged dataframe.

name.description: Staged dataframe name (df_XXXXX_XXXXX) for ilostat_dataframe_query SQL.

datasets.description: The queried datasets, in request order.

items.description: One requested dataset and how its values are classed.

edition.description: The edition the cutoff derives from, e.g. Nov. 2025.

has_aggregates.description: Whether the dataset carries World, regional, or income-group rows.

label.description: Dataset label as ILOSTAT publishes it.

last_update.description: Last upstream update, ISO 8601 without zone offset.

projection_after_year.description: Last year counted as an estimate; modelled rows after it are classed projection.

projection_rule.description: How the cutoff was set: the label's edition, the catalog's latest ILO modelled estimates edition, or the year before the current year.

unit.description: Unit of the values, from ILOSTAT's catalog, already in the multiplier scale; absent only when the catalog lists none.

measure.description: Unit code (PT percent, PS persons, LC local currency, …).

multiplier.description: Power of ten values are expressed in: 0 units, 3 thousands, 6 millions.

type.description: Unit type code (RT rate, NB number, …).

type_label.description: Unit type label; absent when ILOSTAT's structure service could not be read.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `unknown_dataset`: Any dataset ID in dataset_ids, queried or not, is not in the catalog, or a bare indicator code has several frequencies. `unknown_code`: A ref_areas, sex, classif1, classif2, or sources value is not in the ILOSTAT dictionaries. `unknown_area_group`: area_group is not X01, an ILO region or subregion, or a World Bank income group. `aggregates_unavailable`: An X-coded aggregate was requested from a dataset that has no aggregate rows. `invalid_period`: A sub-annual time on a dataset of another frequency, time combined with a range or latest_only, or time_from after time_to. `request_too_broad`: No filters at all and the unfiltered size exceeds the row ceiling. `result_too_large`: The page (offset plus limit) reaches past the row ceiling of a result that holds more rows than the ceiling. `dataset_retired`: Upstream reports a catalog dataset ID as deprecated or invalid. `upstream_busy`: The server-side pacer shed the call, or the ILOSTAT API answered 429 or a challenge page. `catalog_unavailable`: No catalog snapshot has loaded and the load failed, or the first load has not finished within 30 s. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

legend.description: Labels for every code in rows.

classif1.description: classif1 code → label, for every code in rows.

classif2.description: classif2 code → label, for every code in rows.

notes.description: Note code → label, for every code in rows.

obs_status.description: Observation status code → label, for every code in rows.

ref_area.description: Reference area code → label, for every code in rows.

sex.description: Sex code → label, for every code in rows.

source.description: Source code → label, for every code in rows.

next_offset.description: Offset of the next page, set when rows remain past this one; pass it as offset with the same other arguments.

notice.description: A limit past the page cap applied as the cap, datasets left for another call, a latest_only fallback to the latest period per area and dataset, filters that could not narrow a dataset, a unit the catalog does not list, the requested areas that returned no rows and why, why nothing matched, where the full result is staged, which rows the page holds and how to reach the next, or why a first page whose result passes the staging threshold was not staged (dataframes off, staging failed, or the result passes the row ceiling).

remaining_dataset_ids.description: Requested datasets past the first 3, as canonical IDs in request order; not fetched in this call. Pass them as dataset_ids with the same filters to get them. Absent when every requested dataset was queried.

row_count.description: Rows in the result — exact when summary.complete is true; otherwise the rows read before reading stopped past this page, which the result holds at least.

rows.description: This page: at most limit rows from offset, in upstream's order (under per-series latest_only, each series' latest rows, series in the order first seen). A staged dataframe holds every row.

basis.description: reported (national or institutional source), modelled_estimate (ILO modelled, up to the cutoff), or projection (ILO modelled, after it).

best_source.description: Whether this is the preferred source; set only when secondary sources were requested.

classif1.description: First breakdown code, when the dataset has one.

classif2.description: Second breakdown code, when the dataset has one.

sex.description: Sex code; absent when the dataset has no sex breakdown.

value.description: Value in the dataset unit; absent when upstream sent none.

summary.description: Summary over every row read, not just the page.

areas_without_rows.description: Every requested area (ref_areas plus area_group members) that returned no rows, per queried dataset, in the order sent; empty when each returned rows. Absent when complete is false, no area was requested, or the result has no rows.

items.description: One requested area with no rows from one queried dataset.

dataset_id.description: Queried dataset the area returned no rows from.

reason.description: not_covered: absent from the dataset's area list in its SDMX structure. no_rows: listed there, but no rows for these filters and period; every entry is no_rows when that list is unavailable, which notice says.

modelled_estimate.description: ILO modelled estimates up to the cutoff.

projection.description: ILO modelled values after the cutoff.

reported.description: Values from a national or institutional source.

complete.description: True when the read reached the end of the result (always under per-series latest_only, whose history is read whole); false when reading stopped past this page, so the counts cover only the rows read.

period_max.description: Latest period; absent on zero rows.

period_min.description: Earliest period; absent on zero rows.

ref_areas.description: Distinct reference areas in the rows read.

truncated.description: True when rows remain past this page; next_offset continues.

title: Query ILOSTAT observations
